title: Nobody Told Me That a government employee with a suspicious sword in a World Where Paperwork Is Magic
synopsis: A part-time villain accepts a mysterious job and discovers that the job is to manage the hero's retirement fund. The story unfolds in The Republic of Unnecessary Kingdoms, where every spell requires a registered purpose. The central problem is an ancient prophecy that keeps changing its punctuation. Toma Merrin wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A part-time villain accepts a mysterious job and discovers that the job is to manage the hero's retirement fund.
authorNotes: I intended to write a dignified fantasy epic. The characters disagreed.

world.name: The Republic of Unnecessary Kingdoms
world.rule: Every spell requires a registered purpose.
world.oddity: The borders move whenever someone files the correct form.
world.magic: People cast spells by declaring extremely specific exceptions to ordinary physics.
world.threat: an ancient prophecy that keeps changing its punctuation

chapters.title: I Regret Discovering the Royal Mistake — Toma Merrin POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Toma Merrin POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Toma Merrin arrived at the road that moved intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
The road changes its destination while everyone is still walking on it.
Toma Merrin wanted to believe there was a simple answer.
The important object was a map. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Toma Merrin checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Republic of Unnecessary Kingdoms followed one inconvenient rule: Every spell requires a registered purpose.
The road bent left, reconsidered, and politely delivered them somewhere else.
For approximately twelve seconds, that belief survived.
A second person arrived carrying information about the dungeon's legal claim. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the map. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Toma Merrin wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Toma Merrin has a private connection to the oldest dungeon.
The mystery remained open, although Toma Merrin now had one useful fact: someone was treating the dungeon's legal claim as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Toma Merrin made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
